title: Learning from Feedback
description: Study outcome and process supervision, reward design and specification gaming, reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, and generalization and distribution shift. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Outcome and process supervision
lessons.description: Describe how outcome-only and step-level review would differ.
lessons.conceptOverview: Outcome supervision evaluates final success; process supervision evaluates intermediate steps under a labeling scheme. Step labels may improve diagnostic detail but are costly and can encode evaluator mistakes.
lessons.whyItMatters: Final correctness can hide faulty intermediate work.

lessons.title: Reward design and specification gaming
lessons.description: Add checks that tie reward to the actual result and side effects.
lessons.conceptOverview: A reward is a proxy for the desired behavior. Optimizing it can expose loopholes, especially when formatting or test shortcuts receive credit without genuine task completion.
lessons.whyItMatters: Reward design must resist shortcuts unrelated to task success.

lessons.title: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards
lessons.description: Design held-out tests and inspect generalization beyond the reward fixtures.
lessons.conceptOverview: Some tasks provide mechanically checkable outcomes, such as passing tests or exact mathematical constraints. The reward remains limited by the coverage and correctness of the verifier.
lessons.whyItMatters: Verifiable rewards are only as strong as their verification coverage.

lessons.title: Generalization and distribution shift
lessons.description: Create controlled variations that preserve the mathematical task.
lessons.conceptOverview: Training success may depend on familiar templates or tools. Evaluate new structures and conditions to distinguish transferable methods from memorized patterns.
lessons.whyItMatters: Generalization tests should vary superficial and structural features.
